title: Two-Way Tables and Relative Frequency
seo_title: Grade 8 Two-Way Tables Worksheets: Totals, Relative Frequency and Association
standard_text: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 two-way table worksheets: read cells and totals, complete missing values, find relative frequencies of the whole table, rows and columns, and decide if two categories are associated. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A two-way table counts by two categories. Divide a count by the right total to get a relative frequency.
key_sub: “Of the Grade 7 students” → divide by the Grade 7 total. Compare percents to see an association.
body_html:
Two-way tables

A two-way table counts people (or things) by two categories at once. Each cell is one combination. The totals are at the end of each row and column.

Plays a sportNo sportTotal
Grade 7302050
Grade 8451560
Total7535110

Relative frequency

Divide a count by a total. Choose the total that matches the question:

QuestionDivide byExample
What percent of everyone…?grand total30 ÷ 110 ≈ 27.3%
Of the Grade 7 students, what percent…?the Grade 7 row total30 ÷ 50 = 60%
Of those who play a sport, what percent…?the column total30 ÷ 75 = 40%
Example

Is grade associated with playing a sport?

Grade 7: 30 ÷ 50 = 60% play.

Grade 8: 45 ÷ 60 = 75% play.

Answer: Yes, Grade 8 students are more likely to play (75% vs 60%).

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by the grand total when the question says “of the Grade 7 students”.
  • Comparing counts when the groups are different sizes. Compare percents.
  • Reading the wrong row or column. Put a finger on each label.

faq.a: A table that counts data by two categories at the same time, such as grade level and whether a student plays a sport.
A count divided by a total, written as a fraction, decimal or percent.

faq.q: How do you know if there is an association in a two-way table?
faq.a: Find the row (or column) percents. If they are very different between groups, there is an association.

faq.q: Which total do I divide by?
faq.a: Use the total of the group named in the question: the grand total for 'of everyone', a row total for 'of the boys', a column total for 'of those who…'.

What is a relative frequency?
c: A count divided by a total, as a fraction or percent
The biggest count
The total of a row
The difference between two counts
